column4: Moses’ prayer رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى is the section’s explicit parallel for a breast expanded before the burdened task is addressed.
Moses next asks وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى; this ayah supplies the ease immediately following the opened breast of 20:25.
Moses asks وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِى, naming the burden-sharing minister whom the section contrasts with the direct removal of the Prophet’s wizr.
Moses asks ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى; Aaron’s role is to strengthen the support that bears the task, making the section’s minister/back connection concrete.
وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى states what the minister is for: sharing Moses’ affair, unlike the solitary addressee whose burden God removes in surah 94.
God says He made Aaron a وَزِيرًا with Moses; this is the other explicit Quranic naming of the helper through the word the section links to burden-bearing.
God answers Moses, سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ; strengthening his arm through Aaron precisely stages a helper enabling the burdened speaker to stand and act.
كَلَّا لَا وَزَرَ uses the section’s secondary sense of wazar, “refuge,” and denies every shelter before the destination named in 75:12.
إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ completes “no refuge” with the same إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ direction that closes surah 94.
The rider settles عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِۦ and then remembers the Lord’s favor; back, upright settling, remembrance, and benefaction occur in the section’s order.
The mounted traveler says وَإِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ, turning the ride on an animal’s back into movement toward the Lord.
فَمَن شَرَحَ ٱللَّهُ صَدْرَهُۥ لِلْإِسْلَامِ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ directly joins God’s opening of the breast to the divine light in the section’s dictionary gloss.
God يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُۥ لِلْإِسْلَامِ, while the contrary breast is ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا as though climbing upward; it gives both expansion and its bodily reversal.
وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَٱلْأَغْلَٰلَ reproduces the section’s decisive action: a divinely sent messenger puts down the burden and restraints carried by people.
حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلْحَرْبُ أَوْزَارَهَا brings the section’s two words together: war itself “puts down” its awzār, picturing hardship ending as an unloaded burden.
وَهُمْ يَحْمِلُونَ أَوْزَارَهُمْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِمْ explicitly places awzār on backs, the literalized moral load from which the section’s addressee is released.
Whoever turns from ذِكْرِى يَحْمِلْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وِزْرًا; remembrance refused becomes the very burden the section opposes to elevated remembrance.
وَسَآءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ حِمْلًا names the enduring load’s bad weight and completes the burden introduced in 20:100.
حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا stages material loads being carried and then cast down, though their unloading leads into the calf episode.
Those charged to make scripture known نَبَذُوهُ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ; revelation is forgotten behind the back rather than its remembrance being raised and heard.
A group نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ ... كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ, repeating the section’s image of a remembered book displaced behind the back.
The donkey يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَارًا bears books as bodily cargo without receiving their guidance, joining the section’s back-load and forgotten-remembrance images.
Pregnant women’s term lasts أَن يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ, and the ayah concludes يَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِنْ أَمْرِهِۦ يُسْرًا; laying down a pregnancy and ease meet in one verse.
حَتَّىٰ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ and وَإِن تَعَاسَرْتُمْ فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُۥٓ أُخْرَىٰ join delivery, nursing, and mutual difficulty in the section’s second birth scene.
A person whose provision is restricted spends accordingly, then سَيَجْعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا; its “after” sharpens surah 94’s stronger “with.”
وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلَىٰ مَيْسَرَةٍ makes debt a carried constriction and commands respite until spacious ease arrives.
حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرْهًا وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًا gives the section’s dictionary movement literally: a child is borne as hardship and then laid down in birth.
حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُۥ وَهْنًا عَلَىٰ وَهْنٍ describes the mother’s weakening load and ends أَنِ ٱشْكُرْ لِى ... إِلَىَّ ٱلْمَصِيرُ, moving from carried weight to grateful return.
Pregnancy passes from حَمْلًا خَفِيفًا to فَلَمَّآ أَثْقَلَت, whereupon the parents call their Lord; bodily heaviness itself turns the bearers toward the benefactor.
The nursing settlement says لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا and forbids either parent being harmed through the child, defining ease within the weight of care.
Mary’s mother says إِنِّى وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ; وَضَعَ here is exactly the childbirth sense of “put down” developed from the section’s unloading verb.
Cattle تَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ to a distant land reachable only بِشِقِّ ٱلْأَنفُسِ, making the caravan back, load, road, and hardship one literal scene.
وَلِتَبْلُغُوا۟ عَلَيْهَا حَاجَةً فِى صُدُورِكُمْ وَعَلَيْهَا ... تُحْمَلُونَ unusually joins a need held in breasts with being carried on animals.
إِنَّا سَنُلْقِى عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا presents revelation to the same prophetic addressee as a weighty word, the demanding counterpart to removal of his burden.
Had the Quran descended on a mountain, it would be خَٰشِعًا مُّتَصَدِّعًا; a structure splits beneath revelatory weight where the section’s relieved back can stand.
The heavens, earth, and mountains refuse أَن يَحْمِلْنَهَا, but the human حَمَلَهَا; the Trust supplies the cosmic boundary for what a bearer can take on.
The prayer لَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَآ إِصْرًا ... وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ asks the Lord not to impose a back-breaking burden.
مَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰ denies that revelation was sent to make the prophetic addressee wretched; 20:3 identifies it instead as remembrance.
إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ completes 20:2’s removal of distress with remembrance, matching the section’s descent of burden and ascent of dhikr.
وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ directly fuses two of the section’s meetings: ease is made for remembrance.
The repeated يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ makes ease and retained, voiced remembrance a recurring Quranic law rather than a single event.
This third refrain again joins divinely made ease to dhikr, paralleling the section’s move from an eased load to elevated remembrance.
The fourth يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ completes the repeated meeting of ease and remembrance.
فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ joins ease, the addressee’s audible tongue, and remembrance.
سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنسَىٰ promises the prophetic addressee remembrance rather than what is lost behind the back; 87:8–9 continue with ease and reminding.
وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ turns divine action upon the addressee into a course of ease, between the promise not to forget and the command to remind.
فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ makes the divinely eased recipient act, reproducing the section’s shift from receiving God’s acts to obeying a command.
After human formation and measuring, ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ makes the birth-path easy, a concise nonlexical counterpart to the section’s childbirth-ease meeting.
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ makes a person’s giving and God-conscious response lead into divinely granted ease.
إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا names the section’s final posture exactly in other words: strenuous work whose direction is the Lord.
No thirst, نَصَبٌ, or hunger suffered فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ goes unrecorded; this is explicitly Lord-directed fatigue rather than fatigue from a back’s load.
Houses God permits أَن تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُ join raising, voiced remembrance, and a name in one construction.
God and the angels bless the Prophet, then believers are commanded صَلُّوا۟ عَلَيْهِ; his mention is made public and continually voiced by divine act and human response.
Abraham asks وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ, a “truthful tongue” among later peoples that states the remembered, audible name image without رَفَعَ.
وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا combines lasting renown with height, closely matching the section’s status, voice, and memory senses of elevated dhikr.
وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ allows dhikr to mean the addressee’s honor or renown as well as reminder, the semantic meeting developed in the section.
The addressee is commanded to rise for extra night worship so that his Lord may raise him مَقَامًا مَّحْمُودًا; exertion and elevated prophetic station are causally joined.
أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلْإِبِلِ introduces the camel whose back and saddle underlie the section’s caravan image; the next three ayat supply raising, erecting, and spreading.
وَإِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ contributes the raised structure in the camel–mountain–earth sequence that mirrors the section’s construction verbs.
وَإِلَى ٱلْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ uses the section’s dictionary sense of nasb exactly: mountains are lifted and set upright.
وَإِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ completes the sequence with the earth spread flat, corresponding to the section’s repeated image of expansion.
The wall يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُ meets both sides of the section’s posture: a structure about to collapse is made upright.
The shoot فَـَٔازَرَهُۥ ... فَٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِ is strengthened by support until it stands on its stem, a living analogue of help restoring uprightness.
وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا joins name-remembrance with deliberate, exclusive direction toward the Lord.
People whom trade does not distract عَن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ enact the section’s worker whose occupations remain ordered toward remembrance; 24:36 supplies raised houses and the voiced name.
إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ is the closest verbal counterpart to the final command: desire is explicitly directed toward “our Lord.”
After saying God and His Messenger sufficed them, the speakers say إِنَّآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ رَٰغِبُونَ; received provision becomes desire directed back to its giver.
وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا describes prophets calling God in desire and fear, giving the section’s directed رغبة a worshipful stance.
وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا makes the heart an emptied vessel, while God’s binding it shows emptiness made fit to hold a faithful purpose.
سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ ٱلثَّقَلَانِ uses faragha for deliberate attention to an affair, the section’s secondary sense, but here as a warning from the divine speaker.
رَبَّنَآ أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا pictures patience poured from a vessel and immediately asks for firm feet, joining emptying with steadfast posture toward God.
رَبَّنَآ أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا asks the Lord to pour patience upon threatened believers and let them die submitted, combining vessel imagery with unwavering direction.
أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا is a literal command to pour molten copper over the newly erected barrier, preserving the bucket-emptying sense beside purposeful work.
وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ makes “to your Lord” the final endpoint, the destination implicit in the section’s commanded desire.
إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ gives the same addressee and direction as the section’s close, now explicitly as return.
The three find أَن لَّا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيْهِ; constriction gives way to the discovery that refuge from God lies only in turning to Him.
The messenger says no one can protect him from God and he will find no مُلْتَحَدًا apart from Him, a direct semantic counterpart to لَا وَزَرَ and Lordward direction.
مَا لَكُم مِّن مَّلْجَإٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ repeats the no-refuge boundary and commands response to the Lord before that day.
إِنَّآ أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ is a divine “We” gift to the addressee; 108:2 then changes him from recipient to commanded actor, exactly the section’s structural turn.
فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَٱنْحَرْ answers divine giving with effort explicitly “for your Lord,” paralleling the relieved recipient’s Lord-directed action.
وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ recalls God relieving the same addressee’s need; the later commands make received benefaction produce action.
وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ commands the recipient to voice his Lord’s favor, meeting elevated audible remembrance and the final turn to the benefactor.
After divine help and completed victory, فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ turns the addressee from recipient into an active worshipper of his Lord.
فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُم مَّنَٰسِكَكُمْ فَٱذْكُرُوا ٱللَّهَ commands remembrance once rites are completed, a close procedural parallel to “when you are free, exert yourself.”
فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱذْكُرُوا ٱللَّهَ standing, sitting, and reclining makes completion immediately open into another intentional act of remembrance.
The call to remembrance commands فَٱسْعَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ وَذَرُوا۟ ٱلْبَيْعَ; ordinary work is emptied out for deliberate Lordward effort.
فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ sends worshippers back to work while retaining وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًا, a complementary completion-and-new-task sequence.
فَلْيَعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَيْتِ directs the beneficiaries to their Lord; 106:4 names the hunger and fear He removed.
ٱلَّذِىٓ أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ وَءَامَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍ grounds the command to worship in burdens relieved by the benefactor.
A “good loan” is followed by وَٱللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْصُطُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ, joining debt, constriction/expansion, and return to God.
Immediately after the distressed debtor and remission in 2:280, this ayah says تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ and every soul is paid in full.
وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ يَضِيقُ صَدْرُكَ names the same addressee’s constricted breast; 15:98–99 answer it with Lord-directed worship.
فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ turns the constricted breast of 15:97 into commanded bodily worship toward the Lord.
وَٱعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَكَ ٱلْيَقِينُ makes the response to chest-constriction sustained labor for the Lord.
Moses says وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ; constricted breast, blocked voice, and Aaron’s help converge.
هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ states the divine tranquility entering hearts that the section’s dictionary gloss uses to explain breast-opening.
أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ joins remembrance to settled hearts, supplying the inner repose of the section’s widened breast.
Whoever desires the Hereafter وَسَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا has their striving appreciated; desire and labor receive value from their chosen direction.
Remain with those who call their Lord يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ and do not look past them toward worldly adornment; it fixes desire’s direction against the worldly alternative.
إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ makes generous exertion an exclusive seeking of the Most High Lord’s face.
The Hour makes كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا lay down her pregnancy in terror; it is childbirth-as-unloading under catastrophe rather than merciful ease.
مَّن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا shows that opening a breast is directionally neutral as an image; here its content is unbelief, opposite the section’s Lordward end.
The one يَمْشِى مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ is opposed to one يَمْشِى سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ; bent and upright postures become moral directions.
عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ depicts laboring, exhausted people entering fire; its nasb is toil without the fruitful Lordward orientation of the section’s command.
لَا تَرْفَعُوا۟ أَصْوَٰتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ ٱلنَّبِىِّ sets a boundary: God raises the Prophet’s heard mention, while believers may not raise their own voices over his.
وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ limits the minister image: moral burden cannot simply be transferred, and the ayah ends with return to your Lord.
The repeated وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ marks personal responsibility, distinguishing divine removal of a burden from another person carrying it.
وَإِن تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا لَا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌ makes the boundary bodily: even a near relation cannot shoulder the heavily laden person’s load.
No bearer bears another’s burden, then إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ; individual load and Lordward return meet as a limit on human burden-sharing.
أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ is recalled as part of Moses’ and Abraham’s scrolls, reinforcing the boundary beside the section’s Moses–minister scene.
Misleaders يَحْمِلُوا۟ أَوْزَارَهُمْ ... وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُم; their added burdens arise from causing others’ error, not innocent transfer.
وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالًا مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ answers the false offer to carry others’ sins with accumulated loads of responsibility.
يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ states ease and hardship as opposed divine intentions, illuminating surah 94’s more intimate coexistence “with.”
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ paradoxically “eases” the miser toward difficulty, showing that facilitation takes its value from the end toward which one turns.
بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا names the rival direction for the desire and effort ordered toward the Lord in the section.
وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ gives the enduring object opposed to nearer life, following the same passage’s ease and command to remember.
مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ receives only the hastened worldly allotment; 17:19 reverses both the object of desire and the quality of striving.
The harvest of the Hereafter is increased, while one who wants حَرْثَ ٱلدُّنْيَا receives some with no Hereafter share; work’s yield follows desire’s direction.
After God removes human harm مَرَّ كَأَن لَّمْ يَدْعُنَآ, reversing the section’s relieved person who rises and turns deliberately to the benefactor.
After God removes the harm, a group يُشْرِكُونَ بِرَبِّهِمْ; release from weight leads away from the Lord instead of back to Him.
When God rescues distressed sailors to land أَعْرَضْتُمْ, a sharp maritime reversal of the rider who remembers favor and returns toward the Lord.
A distressed person calls رَبَّهُۥ مُنِيبًا إِلَيْهِ, but after receiving favor نَسِىَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ; direction collapses into forgetting.
People call their Lord مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ under harm, but after mercy a faction associates partners; the turn to the giver fails once the burden lifts.
After the heavy pregnancy’s prayer and a sound child, جَعَلَا لَهُۥ شُرَكَآءَ; it reverses grateful Lordward movement after a load is safely delivered.
Were God to بَسَطَ ٱلرِّزْقَ without measure, people would transgress; expansion itself needs a divinely fitted limit and is not unqualified ease.
وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى places released speech between opened breast/eased task and requested minister, anticipating the section’s sound sense of dhikr.
يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى gives the purpose of Moses’ released tongue: words must become heard and retained by others, complementing elevated remembrance.
هَٰرُونَ أَخِى identifies the family member asked for as minister and prepares the strengthening function stated in 20:31.
قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ confirms that the linked requests for expanded breast, ease, and a supporting minister were divinely granted.
Moses calls Aaron أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا and asks that he be sent as support, connecting the helper to audible speech as well as shared burden.
أَيْنَ ٱلْمَفَرُّ voices the fleeing human’s search; its own contribution is the question that “no refuge” answers in 75:11.
The Ark contains سَكِينَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ and is تَحْمِلُهُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ, joining a carried container with Lord-given tranquility rather than oppressive cargo.
وَمَا تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنثَىٰ وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ preserves both bearing and laying down a pregnancy under divine knowledge.
وَمَا تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنثَىٰ وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ repeats pregnancy as a burden eventually put down, though ease is not stated here.
يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمْ grounds divine lightening in human weakness, a general statement of the load-removing act pictured in the section.
The command to strive for God is paired with وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ, combining Lordward exertion with the denial of constricting burden.
مَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ presents ritual commands as purification rather than constriction, supporting the section’s distinction between burden and directed work.
Moses asks لَا تُرْهِقْنِى مِنْ أَمْرِى عُسْرًا; difficulty in an affair is described as something laid heavily upon him.
فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا supplies the easy outcome for the human whose labor is explicitly toward the Lord in 84:6.
A revealed book فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ can mean both reminder and the hearers’ honor, echoing the section’s deliberate preservation of dhikr’s several senses.
وَرَفَعْنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا makes raising a person mean elevated station, clarifying the rank sense within “raising” the addressee’s mention.
يَرْفَعِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ... دَرَجَٰتٍ uses divine raising for rank rather than physical height, one component of the section’s semantic meeting.
وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَٰتٍ places differing elevated ranks among messengers, the prophetic-status dimension of the raised mention.
وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِمَا فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ says Moses and Aaron are left in later memory; 37:120 voices that enduring mention.
سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ is the actual sound preserved among later peoples, and it concerns the same prophet–minister pair developed in the section.
Those who يَغُضُّونَ أَصْوَٰتَهُمْ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ enact the human lowering of voice that complements the boundary in 49:2.
سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى commands a voiced divine name together with height, an inverse but related meeting of name, sound, and elevation.
فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَّرْفُوعَةٌ supplies a raised object; the cup “placed” in 88:14 completes the vertical verb-pair found in the section.
وَأَكْوَابٌ مَّوْضُوعَةٌ supplies the placed object beside the raised couches, a concrete lexical miniature of load put down and mention raised.
وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ pairs raising with setting down, though the objects are sky and balance rather than name and burden.
إِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ ٱلْقَوَاعِدَ makes raising a construction act and immediately turns the builders to their Lord in a prayer for acceptance.
رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّىٰهَا depicts a built canopy raised and made proportionate; 79:30 supplies the complementary spreading of earth.
وَٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ دَحَىٰهَا contributes the spread ground beneath 79:28’s raised heaven, echoing the section’s building-and-expansion cluster.
وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا بِأَيْي۟دٍ presents divine building and expansive power; 51:48 turns to the earth made spread beneath it.
وَٱلْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَٰهَا pictures the earth spread like furnishing, a cosmic counterpart to the section’s garment and opened-space imagery.
لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًا makes nasb the fatigue of Moses’ journey, close to the road-weariness distinguished from a burdened back.
Job’s أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ preserves nasb as afflicting exhaustion rather than the section’s commanded exertion.
لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ marks the final abode as free of fatigue, a boundary beyond the present Lord-directed work.
لَا يَمَسُّهُمْ فِيهَا نَصَبٌ likewise removes all weariness from the garden, distinguishing enduring rest from present exertion.
Those who spend the night لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَٰمًا embody bodily, Lord-directed exertion, including the upright stance implied by fanṣab.
The addressee is told he will find no مُلْتَحَدًا apart from God after reciting revelation, another refuge-word supporting the section’s semantic link from wazar to Lord.
The threatened magicians answer إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ; 7:126 then turns that declared return into a prayer for poured patience.
The magicians again say إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ while facing punishment, making Lordward return the direction that holds through imposed hardship.
فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ joins divinely made ease to the addressee’s tongue so that proclamation can warn and give good news.
أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَـَٔاوَىٰ begins the same addressee’s catalogue of received divine acts, which later changes into commands.
وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلًّا فَهَدَىٰ continues God’s acts upon a receptive addressee before the surah’s closing imperatives.
فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ is the first commanded action arising from the favors in 93:6–8, structurally parallel to surah 94’s turn.
وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ continues the recipient’s new responsibility before the final command to voice the Lord’s favor.
وَضَآئِقٌۢ بِهِۦ صَدْرُكَ addresses the Prophet’s breast constricted by demands placed on his proclamation, the experienced reverse of divinely opened space.
فَلَا يَكُن فِى صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِّنْهُۥ denies constriction in the messenger’s breast so that he can warn with the revealed book.
The Quran is مَوْعِظَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَشِفَآءٌ لِّمَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ, giving a Lord-sent inward remedy corresponding to an opened, tranquil breast.
Every blessing is from God, and under harm فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْـَٔرُونَ; 16:54 tests whether that directed cry survives after relief.
ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ makes provision itself spacious or constrained and adds the risk of rejoicing in nearer life.
إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ supplies the economic expansion and narrowing behind the section’s “provision constrained” scene.
Qarun’s treasure-keys لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُوَّةِ make wealth a load that bends even a strong group; 28:82 reinterprets wealth as provision expanded or constrained by God.
Observers of Qarun confess ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ, turning the story of burdening wealth into recognition of its divine measure.
ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ repeats the section’s economic breadth and restriction as a divine act known by God.
أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ asks readers to see signs in provision’s expansion and constriction.
إِنَّ رَبِّى يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ corrects the belief that wealth proves rank, separating spacious provision from true elevation.
إِنَّ رَبِّى يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ is followed by God replacing what people spend, linking economic breadth to active response.
أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ makes changing provision a sign rather than an autonomous measure of ease.
لَهُۥ مَقَالِيدُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ places breadth and restriction under the Lord’s control.
أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ أَجْرًا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ imagines a demanded payment as debt that weighs the hearers down.
The repeated question فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ again turns a financial liability into bodily heaviness, joining the debt and back-load images.
